To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cell-cell communication model can be approxi- mated by a hierarchy of systems of ODEs, which can be obtained by homogenization with localization, and that the dynamics of these ODEs are qualitatively similar to the dynamics of the full PDE model.
the dynamics of communicating bacteria can be approximated well by ODEs and that the ODE models can be derived by a homogenization procedure with localization.
the dynamics of communicating bacterial cells in a diffusible environment is approximated by a delay ODE, which in turn is approximated by an ODE.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a homogenization problem for a system of coupled PDEs and ODEs, where the homogenization parameter is the size of the cells.
the homogenization of a dynamical model for communicating cells in a medium with small cells and with the approximation of the dynamics of such a model.
the question how a population of communicating cells can be approximated in a diffusive environment by a system of ordinary differential equations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for small cell radius the model is well approximated by a system of $$\mathcal{O}(N^2)$$ coupled ODE’s.
the dynamics of the original PDE model can be approximatively reproduced by a system of ordinary differential equations.
for small $$N$$ and small $$R$$ one can approximate the dynamics by a system of $$O(N^2)$$ ODEs, while for large $$N$$ one can approximate by $$O(N)$$ ODE.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dynamics of the communicating cells in the diffusive environment can be described by an ODE system, which is a consequence of a homogenization process.
we can approximate the dynamics of communicating bacteria by ODEs.
the dynamics of the communicating cells in the diffusive medium can be approximated, for small $$R,$$ by the dynamics of $$N$$ cells in a non-diffusive medium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
for small cell size the dynamics of communicating bacteria is well approximated by a system of ODEs.
the dynamics of a large system of communicating cells in an environment can be described by a system of ODEs, provided that the cells are sufficiently small and sufficiently close to each other.
the ODE approximation is surprisingly accurate for small $$R$$.
